text:
maria: FYI running the browser sample app with the streaming endpoint I see intermittent JSON parse errors right after I click 'Stop' on the app. Happens about 1/4 runs.

alex: can you paste the exact error + steps to repro?

maria: repro steps: 1) open https://internal-samples.local/sse-playground 2) start streaming a long completion (seq len ~1200 tokens) 3) after ~2s click Stop -> UI aborts fetch -> occasionally the last chunk is malformed and UI shows "Unexpected end of JSON input".

maria: error from console: `SyntaxError: JSON.parse: unexpected end of data at line 1 column 234`

jin: this sounds like the browser fetch abort is truncating in-flight chunk leaving a partial JSON token. Our SSE framing expects each event to be a full JSON payload per chunk.

sam: do we treat client-initiated aborts differently in the JS SDK? IIRC we currently call controller.abort() and then suppress retries. That might hide the fact the underlying stream cut mid-chunk.

maria: attaching a minimal curl repro (works server-side):
```
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "https://api.redwood.dev/v1/streams" -d '{"prompt":"long loop","stream":true}'
# press Ctrl+C while it's streaming -> sometimes last line is truncated
```

jin: interesting — server sends `data: {..json..}\n\n` frames. If client aborts mid-frame, the SSE parser yields the partial `data:` line. Our client code then tries JSON.parse on the accumulated buffer and throws.

alex: two actionable options: 1) make parser tolerant to EOF mid-chunk (i.e., ignore final partial data on abort) or 2) make server emit a small terminal marker that is always flushed (`event: stream_end\ndata: \n\n`) so clients can treat incomplete final data as expected. We should also align SDK retry behavior: abort vs network error.

sam: i prefer client-side tolerance + clearer semantics. If abort was initiated by user, app probably doesn't care about trailing partial event. But for accidental disconnects we want retry. We need different classification: `user_abort` vs `network_eof` vs `network_err`.

maria: I hacked a local change to the browser SDK parser: on `fetch` `signal.aborted` treat trailing buffer as dropped and don't JSON.parse it, just emit a `stream_aborted` event. Quick diff:
```js
// sse-parser.js (pseudo)
if (controller.signal.aborted) {
  // drop incomplete last data chunk instead of throwing
  emit('aborted', { reason: 'client' });
  return;
}
```

alex: sounds reasonable. We still need tests for Node-fetch + browsers. Node's `abort-controller` sometimes manifests as `ECONNRESET` which we want to map differently.

jin: I'll add a unit test that simulates an in-flight partial chunk then closes socket. We should assert parser doesn't try to parse partial JSON and instead emits `partial_dropped` event and a non-error close.

sam: and update SDK README: clarify that `fetch().abort()` will not trigger automatic retry; there will be a `stream_aborted` callback on the client. Add note: to force server retry semantics call the SDK `client.cancelAndRetry()` helper (we'll implement).

maria: small workaround for the sample app: when user hits Stop, wait 50ms before aborting to allow TCP buffers to flush. That reduced failures for me. Not a real fix though.

alex: can someone open a PR with: parser change, tests, docs, and a changelog entry. Label with `area:sdk-browser` and `severity:low`? Also add an integ test in samples that exercises the UX flow.

jin: created draft PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-js/pull/492 (WIP) — parser change + unit tests. Needs review.

deploy-bot: Deployment queued for canary; no user-facing breaking changes expected.

sam: awesome. followups: - add telemetry event when we drop a partial chunk (so we can measure how often) - coordinate with platform team on server flush guarantees when using proxy/buffers

maria: thanks all — will try PR on sample app UX once the SDK signature lands. :rocket:
